summary: HTTP (Hispanic Tech and Telecommunications Partnerships) urges the FCC to preserve the current E‑Rate framework, oppose limiting support to rural areas, and reject using the program to dictate educational policy. The comment argues that E‑Rate should remain available to all eligible schools and libraries, not just rural ones, and that educational policy decisions such as screen‑time limits should be left to schools and families rather than the FCC. The comment opposes FCC‑proposed screen‑time limits, arguing that such policy should remain under local control.
